title: By this city, Makkah.
subtitle: An oath by the sacred city, the Mother of Towns
then: Ibn Abbas said: {idea}this means Makkah.{/idea} Mujahid said the opening No is {trap}a refutation against Quraysh.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}Allah made this city sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth.{/idea}
now: Maybe you have stood in front of the Kaaba, or watched it on a livestream at 3am, or just turned toward it five times a day. {idea}Allah swears by that city.{/idea} The place your prayers face is honored by its Lord.
old: Makkah is a holy place far away from my daily life.
new: The city I turn to in every prayer is one Allah Himself swears by.
try: At your next prayer, pause a moment while facing the qiblah and remember what you are facing.

title: And you, O Prophet ﷺ, live in this city.
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ place in the sacred city
then: Ibn Abbas and many others said this told the Prophet ﷺ it would be {idea}permitted for him to fight in it{/idea}, which the Prophet ﷺ said was {idea}only for one hour of a day{/idea}, after which its sanctity returned. Revealed when Makkah's leaders had {trap}made it lawful for themselves to wrong him.{/trap}
now: You may live somewhere hard: a tense home, a workplace where your values are mocked. {idea}The verse reminds the Prophet ﷺ that Allah sees exactly where he lives and what he faces there.{/idea} He sees your place too.
old: Where I live and what I face there is not noticed by anyone.
new: Allah knows the place I live in and what it costs me to be there.
try: Make a short dua for the place you live and the people in it.

title: By the father, and the child he fathered.
subtitle: Adam and his children, every parent and child
then: Mujahid and many others said: {idea}the begetter is Adam, and what he begot is his children.{/idea} Ibn Kathir: Allah swears by the Mother of Towns, then by its dwellers. Ibn Jarir held it is general: {idea}every father and his children.{/idea}
now: Your father holding you on the first day. You holding your own child, or a nephew, years later. {idea}The chain from Adam runs through you.{/idea} Allah swears by it, so every link matters.
old: Family is just the people I happen to be related to.
new: Parent and child is a bond Allah swears by. My place in it matters.
try: Call or message your father or mother today, or make dua for them if they have passed.

title: We created man into struggle.
subtitle: Hardship is built into human life from the start
then: Ibn Abbas: {idea}he was created while in hardship. Do you not see him?{/idea} and he mentioned birth and teething. Mujahid linked it to {trap}his mother bears him with hardship{/trap}. Said bin Jubayr: in hardship and seeking a living.
now: The rent, the commute, the night feeds, the exams. You keep thinking life will get easy once this one thing is sorted. {idea}Struggle is not a sign something went wrong.{/idea} It is the setting. What matters is what you strive for.
old: If life is this hard, something must be wrong with me.
new: Hardship is the ground I was made to walk on. It is not a failure.
try: Name today's hardest task and offer the effort of it to Allah with a quick intention.

title: Does he think no one has power over him?
subtitle: The illusion of being untouchable
then: Al-Hasan said: {trap}no one is able to take his wealth.{/trap} Qatadah said: {idea}the son of Adam thinks he will not be asked about his wealth, how he earned it and how he spent it.{/idea} Right after being told he was made into struggle.
now: A good salary, a solid pension, a house in your name. It starts to feel like armor. {idea}Every pound or dollar has two questions attached:{/idea} where did it come from, and where did it go?
old: My money is my business. No one can touch it.
new: I will be asked how I earned and spent every bit of it.
try: Look at your last five purchases and ask yourself how you would explain each to Allah.

title: He boasts: I have spent heaps of money.
subtitle: Bragging about spending as if it were virtue

row.title: how and why I spent it

then: Mujahid, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said he says {trap}I spent an abundance of wealth.{/trap} The surah introduction explains: people {trap}admire the one who squanders for display{/trap}, while Allah sees how he earned it and why he spent it.
now: The wedding with the fireworks. The birthday unboxing on social media. The donation announced loudly. {trap}Spending big is easy to brag about.{/trap} {idea}Allah looks at the intention, not the number.{/idea}
old: If I spend a lot, I must be generous.
new: It is not how much I spend, but how and why.
try: Give one gift or charity this week without telling anyone about it.

title: Does he think no one saw him?
subtitle: Allah saw the spending and the motive behind it
then: Mujahid said: {idea}does he think Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not see him?{/idea} After the boast of verse 6, the question cuts through it. The crowd saw the display. {idea}Allah saw the whole story.{/idea}
now: You post the restaurant bill, the new car, the holiday photos. Hundreds of people see. {idea}One sees the credit card debt, the motive, and the person you did not help.{/idea}
old: What people see of me is what counts.
new: Allah sees what is behind the picture I show.
try: Before posting anything today, ask: who am I doing this for?

title: Did We not give him two eyes?
subtitle: The One who gave sight sees everything
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}for him to see with them.{/reward} It answers verse 7 directly. He thinks no one sees him, yet {idea}the One who gave him eyes is asking.{/idea} The surah moves from accountability to blessings.
now: Your eyes read this. They will scroll, read faces, see your children grow. {reward}You did not order them.{/reward} {idea}What you choose to look at with them is the answer to this verse.{/idea}
old: My eyes are mine to look at whatever I like.
new: My eyes are a gift from the One who sees me. I use them for Him.
try: Lower your gaze once today from something you know you should not look at.

title: And a tongue, and two lips?
subtitle: The gift of speech and what it carries
then: Ibn Kathir: a tongue {reward}to speak with and express what is inside him{/reward}, and two lips to help with speaking, eating, and to beautify the face. The same tongue that boasted in verse 6 was a gift.
now: The voice note you sent in anger. The kind word to a cashier. The dua whispered in sujood. {idea}Same tongue, same lips.{/idea} Each word is a way of thanking, or not thanking, the One who gave them.
old: My words are just words. They do not matter much.
new: My tongue is a gift, and every word is a choice to use it well.
try: Say one sincere compliment or thank-you today to someone who does not expect it.

title: And showed him the two roads.
subtitle: Good and evil, both made clear
then: Ibn Masud said: {idea}the good and the evil.{/idea} Ali, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the same. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: {idea}We showed him the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful.{/idea} The ability to tell good from evil is itself a blessing.
now: You stand at a crossroads many times a day: the honest answer or the easy lie, the prayer or the snooze button. {idea}You usually know which is which.{/idea} That knowing is a gift. The choosing is your part.
old: I am not sure what is right, so I cannot be blamed.
new: I was shown both roads. Knowing is a gift, and choosing is mine.
try: At one small choice today, pause and pick the road you know is better.
